strategy.observation: Linear says it powers over 40,000 product teams, so it likely has a broad customer base of exactly the kind of users a product team would want to interview.
strategy.offer_link: That scale makes a participant-recruiting and scheduling service relevant because it could help the product team quickly find and book interviews with existing product-team customers instead of sourcing them manually.
hypotheses: The product team regularly runs customer interviews to shape roadmap decisions.
They may need help targeting specific customer segments such as PMs, engineering leads, or admins.
Scheduling across a distributed customer base may be a bottleneck.
They may prefer a third party to handle outreach and coordination rather than doing it in-house.
strategy.angle: Linear already has 40,000+ product teams using the product, so finding the right customer interview participants should be a real advantage.
strategy.fit_reason: Linear’s audience is itself product teams, which makes customer interviews especially relevant to its Head of Product. A service that recruits and schedules those participants could plausibly save time and improve access to the right users, so the fit is strong.

draft.subject: Customer interviews
draft.body:

I help product teams recruit and schedule customer interview participants. If your team is running interviews this quarter, I can handle the outreach and coordination and get the right users booked faster.

Are you trying to reach a specific customer segment right now?
